cards.method: Johansen procedure + restricted VECM + Phillips-Ouliaris/Engle-Granger residual tests
cards.when: A system of >=2 I(1) series; testing the cointegration rank + extracting beta/alpha, or a residual-based test (coint_phillips_ouliaris, Pu/Pz).
cards.when_not: You need p-values for the rank (go to #24); mixed order I(0)/I(1) (go to #25, ARDL bounds).

alternatives.criterion: You want p-values for the rank + 5 deterministic specs.
Single equation with a mixed order of integration I(0)/I(1).
The rank is known (=1) and you want an unbiased estimate of beta.

output_key_fields: teststat: statistics per rank hypothesis (compare with cval)
cval: critical values 10/5/1% (NOT a p-value)
lambda: eigenvalues
V: normalised cointegrating vectors (beta)
W: loading weights (alpha, speed of adjustment)
PI: Pi = alpha beta'
coint_phillips_ouliaris teststat/cval: Pu or Pz; res = the residuals of the cointegrating regression
cajorls beta/rlm_coef: restricted VECM at rank r
interpretation_traps: coint_johansen gives ONLY critical values, NOT a p-value — compare teststat > cval (#24 documents the same convention).

coint_johansen(type=..) returns ONLY the selected test type per call: teststat/cval hold trace OR max-eigen, not both — to compare trace vs eigen call it TWICE (type='trace' & type='eigen'); by contrast rank_test gives trace AND eigen p-values together in one call.
The K of coint_johansen (lags in levels) = lag+1 of vecm_rank_test (an off-by-one).
KPSS has the opposite polarity among the preconditions: reject H0 ⇒ non-stationary.
Pz is invariant to the normalisation; prefer it when there is no natural dependent variable.
the result serialises to a compact stub → rely on the atomic fields.

cards.method: VECM estimate + Johansen rank_test (ML-only) + rank selection + predict
cards.when: A system VECM with a Johansen rank test WITH p-values, 5 deterministic specs, 2OLS/ML estimation, rank selection by IC, forecasting.
cards.when_not: You need seasonal/exogenous regressors in the Johansen test (#23 only); a single equation of mixed order.

alternatives.criterion: You want seasonal/exogenous regressors or a plain critical-value comparison.
Single equation, mixed order of integration.
Known rank=1, you want an unbiased beta with t-tests.

output_key_fields: beta: cointegrating vectors
alpha: loadings (negative & significant ⇒ valid error correction)
PI: Pi = alpha beta'
rank_test table: trace/eigen stats AND p-values
r: selected rank (the first H0 not rejected at cval)
best_ranks: AIC/BIC/HQ selection
forecast: a matrix, horizon × k (chart data)
interpretation_traps: rank_test REQUIRES estim='ML' — with 2OLS it is blocked (hard gate).
Lag convention: the K of #23 = lag+1 here.
p-values = gamma approximation (Doornik); the effective sample size differs from gretl.

cards.method: ARDL / UECM estimation + PSS bounds F/t-test + RECM + multipliers + coint_eq
cards.when: Single-equation cointegration with regressors of mixed order I(0)/I(1); a bounds test without pre-classification; multipliers/ECM/cointegrating equation.
cards.when_not: Any I(2) series (the bounds test breaks down); multiple cointegrating relations (go to the system Johansen).

alternatives.criterion: You want stochastic counterfactual simulation + residual diagnostics.
System / multiple cointegrating relations.
The level relationship is confirmed, you want an unbiased beta.

output_key_fields: bounds statistic/p_value: atomic fields
tab: statistic + critical bounds I(0)/I(1) + alpha + p-value
parameters/PSS2001parameters: critical value bounds
coefficients/best_order/AIC/BIC/log_lik/nobs
multipliers: lr (default)/sr/interim
recm: restricted ECM (the ECT loading is negative & significant)
coint_eq: fitted cointegrating series (chart-data)
interpretation_traps: Inconclusive region: a statistic between the I(0)/I(1) bounds ⇒ NO conclusion about cointegration.
The default p-value is asymptotic (T=1000, exact=False, deterministic); ONLY exact=True runs a simulation (the configured number of replications, wrapper seed=2025).
The wrong case (1-5) ⇒ the wrong H0; you do not restrict a deterministic term that is not there.
case=5 requires a trend; case=1 requires a model without a constant.

cards.method: Dynamic ARDL/ECM + stochastic simulation + PSS bounds + residual diagnostics
cards.when: A single-equation ARDL/ECM when you want counterfactual shock simulation (response path chart-data) + native PSS bounds + BG/SW residual diagnostics.
cards.when_not: You do not need simulation/diagnostics (go to ARDL); system/multiple relations; I(2) series.

alternatives.criterion: The same PSS bounds, richer multipliers/auto-order, without simulation.
System VECM.
Unbiased estimation of beta.

output_key_fields: coefficients/AIC/BIC/log_lik/nobs/residuals
simulation: a frame with the central path + ll95/ul95 (chart data, only when simulate=True)
fstat/tstat: PSS statistics (NOT a p-value)
f_bounds/t_bounds: named vectors of critical I(0)/I(1) × 10/5/1%
bg_statistic/bg_pvalue: Breusch-Godfrey autocorrelation
sw_statistic/sw_pvalue: Shapiro-Wilk normality
interpretation_traps: dyn_pss_bounds does NOT give a p-value — compare fstat/tstat with the I(0)/I(1) bounds (as in #2).
An inconclusive region between the bounds ⇒ NO conclusion.
data MUST be a plain data_frame, NOT a series (hard gate).
dyn_pss_bounds REQUIRES ec=True (the error-correction form).
simulate=True is Monte Carlo (stochastic) → wrapper seed=2025; a different seed ⇒ different interval bands.
A Breusch-Godfrey rejection ⇒ autocorrelation undermines the validity of the bounds test.
sources: Jordan & Philips 2018 (cointegration testing and dynamic simulation of ARDL models)

cards.method: Modified-OLS cointegrating regressions: FM-OLS / D-OLS / IM-OLS
cards.when: ONE known/assumed cointegrating relation; unbiased, asymptotically efficient estimation of beta with valid t-tests (correcting endogeneity/serial correlation).
cards.when_not: You have not confirmed cointegration (these are estimators, NOT tests); multiple cointegrating vectors (go to a system VECM).

alternatives.criterion: Default; semiparametric long-run variance correction (Phillips-Hansen).
Parametric correction with leads/lags of the differenced regressors, no kernel choice.
Robust without bandwidth tuning; it REPLACES CCR, which this card does not provide.
You want a TEST for the existence of cointegration, not an estimate.

output_key_fields: beta: cointegrating vector (the main objective)
delta: coefficients of the deterministic terms
theta: combined (delta, beta)
sd_theta/t_theta/p_theta: standard error / t / p (only when y is one-dimensional)
residuals: the first FM residual is always missing (structural)
omega_u_v: the conditional long-run variance; Omega: the full long-run variance matrix
bandwidth/kernel: the choices made; for D-OLS the lead_lag order
interpretation_traps: Estimators, NOT tests — they do not decide whether cointegration exists (run #23-#26 first).
the first FM residual is missing by design (not a bug).
t/p-values only for one-dimensional y.
IM-OLS has NO demeaning argument (unlike FM/D).
Align deter (const/trend) with the deterministic spec of the test that confirmed the relation.
IM replaces CCR — do not ask for CCR.

cards.method: Fractionally Cointegrated VAR (Johansen-Nielsen): fractional cointegration with estimated d/b + rank tests (asymptotic + wild bootstrap) + lag selection
cards.when: a system of >=2 series with fractional integration (long memory, non-integer I(d)) -> fractional cointegration; estimating d/b + the cointegrating beta + the adjustment alpha; lag_select -> rank_test -> boot_rank -> estimate (the PRODUCER)
cards.when_not: purely integer I(1) with no long memory -> the integer Johansen procedure (#23/#24); a single equation of mixed order -> #25/#26; hypothesis restrictions and forecasting are omitted

alternatives.criterion: the integer Johansen VECM when d~=1 (standard critical values, simpler)
the integer Johansen WITH p-values
a small sample -> the asymptotic LR rank test is unreliable, you need the wild bootstrap

output_key_fields: fcv_estimate: d/b (fractional params), beta (p x r cointegrating), alpha (p x r adjustment), Pi=alpha*beta', Gamma/Omega/mu, log_lik/fp/SE, roots (re/im/mod), object (the FCVAR_model PRODUCER)
fcv_rank_test: LRstat/pv vectors of length p+1 (entry i -> rank=i-1); the rank is read bottom-up, at the first non-rejected H0; the p-value is 999 or blank when unavailable
fcv_lag_select: aic/bic (+ i_aic/i_bic, the selected lag), pvWNQ/pvWNLM white-noise tests per lag
fcv_boot_rank: LRbs (B simulated LR — chart-data), LRstat (the observed one), pv_bs (the bootstrap p-value = H.pvBS)
interpretation_traps: the raw opt object (~40 fields) is NOT exposed; it is built internally from a curated surface (bounds/restrict_db/constrained/level_param/constants/grid_search)

grid_search defaults to False (a deliberate deviation from the reference default); the switching optimiser converges on its own, and the grid search is an expensive accuracy refinement for local maxima in d and b
the bootstrap p-value is reported in the H_pvBS field; the plain pv field comes back empty
FCVAR does NOT enforce r1<r2 (a silently wrong negative LR) -> the wrapper gates it
full rank r=p -> a singular Hessian in the SE (silenced); it means no rank reduction (stationary fractional differences); r>p -> a cryptic non-conformable arguments error
sources: Johansen & Nielsen 2012 (Econometrica 80:2667-2732, Likelihood inference for a fractionally cointegrated VAR)
Cavaliere, Rahbek & Taylor 2010 (J. Econometrics 158:7-24, wild-bootstrap rank test)
Doornik 2018 (Scand. J. Statist. 45(2), accelerated switching algorithm)
FCVAR 0.1.4 reference manual (FCVARoptions/FCVARestn/FCVARrankTests/FCVARlagSelect/FCVARbootRank) — live-verified via Rd + votingJNP2014 probes
precondition_tools: c02_univariate_forecasting/long_memory_fractional.arfima_gph (estimate the fractional order d — FCVAR vs integer Johansen)

cards.method: Nonlinear (asymmetric) ARDL — NARDL (Shin-Yu-Greenwood-Nimmo) + PSS bounds + CUSUM/CUSUMQ stability
cards.when: Single-equation cointegration with an ASYMMETRIC relation: the regressor acts differently on increases vs decreases (positive/negative partial sums); regressors of mixed order I(0)/I(1); EXACTLY one decomposed regressor; long-run beta+/beta- + a Wald test of asymmetry + PSS bounds + CUSUM/CUSUMQ.
cards.when_not: A symmetric relation (a linear ARDL suffices) -> #25; any I(2) series (the bounds test breaks down); multiple cointegrating relations / a system -> Johansen #23/#24; >1 decomposed regressor (nardl accepts EXACTLY one).

alternatives.criterion: The relation is SYMMETRIC (a linear ARDL/UECM + bounds suffices).
You want stochastic counterfactual simulation + residual diagnostics.
A system / multiple cointegrating relations.

output_key_fields: long_run: a table of long-run coefficients x_p (positive) / x_n (negative) + SE/t/p
asym_lr / asym_sr: the Wald test of asymmetry (statistic, p_value); H0 of asym_lr: beta+ = beta- (long-run symmetry)
ect_coef: the coefficient on the lagged DV (error correction; it must be negative)
fstat / orders / case / k / Nobs; normality (Shapiro) & arch (Engle) htests
nar_bounds: statistic + bounds (a data_frame level/I0/I1 10/5/1%) + decision + report (the raw pssbounds display)
nar_stability: cusum & cusumq -> x/process/lower/upper/breach (chart-data, NOT a plot)
interpretation_traps: Decision (bounds): F > the upper I(1) 5% bound ⇒ cointegration; F < the lower I(0) bound ⇒ none; BETWEEN ⇒ inconclusive (no conclusion).
case: ONLY 3 (unrestricted intercept, no trend) or 5 (+trend) are supported; 1/2/4 -> a cryptic error in nardl (the gate blocks it).
a NON-significant asym_lr ⇒ the asymmetry is NOT justified -> go back to the linear ARDL #25.
nar_fit accepts EXACTLY one decomposed regressor; the bounds test takes k from the fit, following the documented convention.

CUSUM and CUSUMQ take k and n from the selected-model fields, not from the top-level k and n, which stay at 1 and the number of differenced rows when plotting is off — that would give silently wrong bounds.
sources: Shin, Yu & Greenwood-Nimmo 2014 (Festschrift in Honor of Peter Schmidt, Ch.9: Modelling Asymmetric Cointegration and Dynamic Multipliers in a NARDL Framework)
nardl reference manual + source (nardl, pssbounds, cusum, cumsq)

cards.method: Consistent monitoring of stationarity & cointegration (Wagner-Wied): calibration-period estimation + a sequential detector (FM/D/IM-OLS)
cards.when: You have an established cointegration relation (or a stationary series) and you monitor whether it BREAKS DOWN in a later period; estimation only on a break-free calibration sample [1.floor(m*N)] -> detector -> break point.
cards.when_not: A full-sample one-shot test for the existence of cointegration (#23/#25/#26); estimating beta (#27); you cannot assume a break-free calibration period.

alternatives.criterion: A univariate series (level/trend stationarity) rather than a relation.
The default; semiparametric long-run variance correction (Phillips-Hansen).
D-OLS (=DOLS); leads/lags of the differenced regressors.
IM-OLS; integrated-modified, robust without bandwidth tuning at the estimation point.
A full-sample TEST for the existence of cointegration (rank), not sequential monitoring.
ESTIMATING the cointegrating vector beta, not monitoring.

output_key_fields: statistic: the detector value (H_sm)
critical_value: the critical value at signif_level
detected: the DECISION — a break/deviation was detected (boolean)
detection_time: the detection index (blank when there is none; the raw infinite time is not exposed)
statistics_path: the detector path, blank over the calibration period (chart data)
p_value: bounded to ∈ [0.01, 0.1] (not an exact p)
residuals: modified-OLS residuals (cmo_cointegration only)
calibration: the fraction m_frac + the index floor(m*N)
kernel/bandwidth/trend/model: the options that were used
object: the monitor handle (not a producer; a stub once serialised)
interpretation_traps: m = the CALIBRATION fraction ∈ [0.1,0.9]; the last observation = floor(m*N); a bad calibration (containing a break) invalidates the procedure.
p_value is bounded to [0.01,0.1] (0.1=far from rejection, 0.01=strong) — NOT an exact p-value.
detected=False with a blank detection_time (an infinite raw time) means no break, not an error.
model='D'=DOLS, 'IM'=Integrated-Modified; there is NO 'DOLS'/'CCR' token.
Silently wrong: a multi-column y, a gap, or an x whose row count does not match y — the underlying routine only WARNS and returns garbage; hard-gated here.
Fully deterministic (no RNG/bootstrap) -> reproducible without a seed; computational (no register).
sources: Wagner & Wied 2015 (SSRN DOI:10.2139/ssrn.2624657, Monitoring Stationarity and Cointegration)
precondition_tools: c05_cointegration/johansen_restricted_vecm.coint_johansen (cointegration in the calibration period, cmo_cointegration only)

cards.method: Gregory-Hansen cointegration with a structural break
cards.when: testing for cointegration when the relationship itself may have shifted -- standard tests treat a break as evidence against cointegration
cards.when_not: the break date is known (use a dummy in a standard test); there is more than one break, which the test cannot accommodate

alternatives.criterion: no break suspected
one unknown break in the cointegrating relationship
the break date is known

output_key_fields: statistic: the supremum ADF, Za or Zt statistic
break_date: the estimated break
critical_values: from the non-standard distribution the test requires
model: which break specification -- level, trend or regime -- was fitted
interpretation_traps: the critical values are NOT the standard Engle-Granger ones; using them badly over-rejects and manufactures cointegration
the test allows ONE break; with two or more it loses power and can fail to reject when cointegration with breaks is present
the break date is estimated with wide uncertainty and should not be reported as if it were known

cards.method: Likelihood-ratio tests of restrictions on beta and alpha, and weak exogeneity
cards.when: testing whether a cointegrating vector takes the form theory predicts, and whether a variable can be treated as weakly exogenous
cards.when_not: the cointegrating rank is zero, so there is no beta to restrict; the restrictions are not over-identifying and no test exists

alternatives.criterion: theory predicts the long-run relationship
you want to test weak exogeneity or exclusion
both are predicted together

output_key_fields: lr_statistic, p_value, df: the restriction test
beta_restricted: the estimated vector under the restriction
weak_exogeneity: per-variable test that its adjustment coefficient is zero
identified: whether the restrictions just-identify or over-identify
interpretation_traps: beta is identified only up to NORMALISATION; a restriction that merely re-normalises is not testable, and testing it produces a meaningless zero statistic
weak exogeneity means the variable does not adjust to the long-run relationship -- it does not mean the variable is exogenous in any broader sense
the chi-squared distribution requires the restrictions to be over-identifying; with just-identifying restrictions there is nothing to test
sources: Johansen 1995, Likelihood-Based Inference in Cointegrated Vector Autoregressive Models

cards.method: Panel cointegration: Pedroni, Kao and Westerlund
cards.when: testing for a long-run relationship across a panel, where pooling raises power far above what any single country's short series provides
cards.when_not: the panel units are cross-sectionally dependent and the test assumes independence; the time dimension is too short

alternatives.criterion: heterogeneous cointegrating vectors across units
homogeneous cointegrating vector
error-correction based, robust to cross-sectional dependence with bootstrap

output_key_fields: statistics: the panel and group-mean statistics
p_values: asymptotic and, where computed, bootstrap
cross_sectional_dependence: the CD test, which decides whether the asymptotic p-values are usable
n_units, n_periods
interpretation_traps: CROSS-SECTIONAL DEPENDENCE invalidates the asymptotic p-values of Pedroni and Kao; the CD test must be run first and a bootstrap used if it rejects
Pedroni's panel and group-mean statistics answer different questions -- pooled versus average -- and can disagree
these tests assume no structural breaks, and a common break across units looks like an absence of cointegration
sources: Pedroni 1999 (Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics 61:653-670)
Westerlund 2007 (Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics 69:709)

cards.method: Threshold and asymmetric error correction: Hansen-Seo TVECM and Enders-Siklos TAR
cards.when: adjustment toward equilibrium is faster in one direction than the other, or only begins once the disequilibrium is large enough
cards.when_not: adjustment is plainly symmetric and linear; the sample is too short to estimate a threshold and two regimes

alternatives.criterion: adjustment is symmetric
asymmetric adjustment around a threshold
a full threshold vector error-correction system

output_key_fields: threshold: the estimated threshold and its confidence interval
adjustment: speed of adjustment in each regime
linearity_test: test of one regime against two, with a bootstrap p-value
regime_share: observations in each regime
interpretation_traps: the threshold is a NUISANCE PARAMETER NOT IDENTIFIED under the null of linearity, so the test has a non-standard distribution and needs a bootstrap p-value
a regime containing very few observations gives an adjustment coefficient estimated on almost nothing
M-TAR conditions on the change rather than the level of the disequilibrium, and the two versions frequently disagree
sources: Enders & Siklos 2001 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 19:166)

cards.when: estimating a cointegrating vector with a transformation that removes the endogeneity and serial-correlation bias of ordinary least squares
cards.when_not: there is more than one cointegrating vector (-> Johansen); the correction cannot be estimated because the long-run covariance is unstable

alternatives.criterion: the same aim by a different correction
leads and lags instead of a covariance correction
a transformation of the data rather than of the estimator

output_key_fields: params, bse: the corrected cointegrating vector and its standard errors
long_run_covariance: the estimate driving the correction
stability_test: test that the relationship is stable
residuals: the equilibrium error
interpretation_traps: OLS on a cointegrating relationship is CONSISTENT BUT BIASED in finite samples and its t-statistics are invalid; that bias is exactly what these estimators correct
all three corrections depend on a long-run covariance estimate, and they inherit its bandwidth sensitivity
with a single cointegrating vector assumed, the presence of a second invalidates the whole exercise
